runner.text:
# Brief for the coach: what the engine shows, and the change on the table

Nothing has been written yet. Everything below comes from read-only views and a dry run of the proposed amendment; the current program is still the one adopted on 1 Nov 2026.

## 1. The program as it stands

Title: "Five compounds around the PT Tuesday". Hypertrophy emphasis, home-based, six training days with Thursday off, two-week rotation (A and B) that differs only in the Tuesday PT session.

**The week**
- Monday: Overhead press, back and arms (budget 75 min).
- Tuesday: PT at the gym. Week A chest and back (estimated 6 chest, 6 lat, 3 biceps hard sets); week B legs and core (estimated 6 quad, 4 glute, 4 ab hard sets).
- Wednesday: Pull-up volume and core (75 min), before the lunchtime run.
- Friday: Strict pull-up test, squat and legs (75 min).
- Saturday: Bench, back and arms (90 min).
- Sunday: Deadlift and legs (90 min).
- Standing/optional: a conditioning circuit (done on a spare evening) and a daily hang.

**Monday session**
- Overhead press: warm-ups of 5 and 3, then a top single set of 5 at RPE 8, then 4 back-off sets of 6 at 85 % of the top set. 180 s rest. Cues: glutes and abs tight, bar starts on the shoulders, head through once the bar passes the forehead.
- Dumbbell chest-supported row: 4 sets of 8–12 at RPE 8, 120 s rest, double progression.
- Lateral raise and rear-delt fly as a pair: 3 sets each of 12–15 at RPE 8, 60 s rest.
- Kettlebell swing finisher: 8 sets of 10 at RPE 7, one set at the top of each minute, 45 s rest, starting at 40 lb.

**Wednesday session**
- Scapular pull-ups: 2 activation sets of 6–8 at RPE 5.
- Negative pull-ups: 3 sets of 2–4 at RPE 8, 120 s rest, 4–5 s lower; once every set hits 4, lengthen to 6 s, then 8 s, then add the vest.
- Band pull-ups: 4 sets of 5–8 at RPE 8, 90 s rest; at the top of the range on every set, move to a lighter band.
- Flexed-arm hang: 2 holds of 20 s.
- Lying leg raise 3 sets of 10–15 and suitcase carry 4 holds of 30 s, as a pair, 60 s rest.
- Single-leg calf raise: 3 sets of 10–15 at RPE 8.

**Friday session**
- Strict pull-up: one max-effort single (RPE 10), same grip every test, a couple of dead hangs first.
- Back squat: warm-ups of 5, 3 and 2, top set of 5 at RPE 8, 4 back-offs of 5 at 85 %. 180 s rest.
- Romanian deadlift: 3 sets of 6–10 at RPE 8, 150 s rest.
- Dumbbell split squat: 3 sets of 8–12 at RPE 8, 90 s rest.
- Seated dumbbell shoulder press 3 × 8–12 and single-leg calf raise 3 × 10–15 as a pair, 75 s rest.
- Ab wheel: 3 sets of 6–12 at RPE 8.

**Saturday session**
- Bench press: warm-ups of 8, 5 and 3, top set of 5 at RPE 8, 4 back-offs of 6 at 85 %. 180 s rest.
- Barbell bent-over row: 4 sets of 6–10 at RPE 8, 120 s rest.
- Dumbbell incline bench: 3 sets of 8–12 at RPE 8, 120 s rest.
- Dip negatives: 3 sets of 3–5 at RPE 8, 90 s rest, 4–5 s lower; once every set reaches 5, lengthen to 6 s, then 8 s, then add the vest.
- Overhead triceps extension 3 × 10–15 and lateral raise 3 × 12–15 as a pair, 60 s rest.

**Sunday session**: deadlift (top set and back-offs, 210 s rest) and legs, including a farmer's walk starting at 50 lb. The full line list was cut off in the output.

**Targets and deload policy**
- 10 hard sets per muscle per week. Per lift: pull-up 1, bench 5, overhead press 5, deadlift 4, back squat 5.
- Light week after at most 6 hard weeks: 40 % of working sets cut, loads kept, RPE capped at 8, priority lifts tested.

## 2. Where Joe is

- **Bench**: estimated max 174.9 lb; best logged 160.94 × 3 on 14 Apr 2026; 0.32 × bodyweight short of the 1.25 × BW target.
- **Overhead press**: estimated max 85.15 lb; best 93 × 5 on 10 Jul 2026; 0.24 × BW short of 0.75 × BW.
- **Back squat**: estimated max 231.48 lb; best 220.46 × 1 on 13 Oct 2026; 0.32 × BW short of 1.5 × BW.
- **Deadlift**: no current estimate; best 200 × 5 on 11 Apr 2026; 0.9 × BW short of 2 × BW.
- **Strict pull-up**: best 3 reps on 29 Mar 2026; currently 1; 2 reps short of five.
- **Phase**: maintenance, target 0.0 % bodyweight change a week, observed −0.13 % a week. Flagged as not on target, but that is a small drift on a few days of data, not a problem yet.

**Monday 2 Nov, as logged**
- Overhead press at 68 lb: 5 reps at RPE 7.5, then 6, 8, 8, 8 at RPE 6. Estimated max from it: 85.0 lb. The back-offs were prescribed as sets of 6 at 85 %; he did 8s and reported them easy.
- Chest-supported row, 20 lb per hand: 6, 12, 12 at RPE 8, 7, 7.5.
- Lateral raise, 5 lb per hand: 15, 15, 15 at RPE 6, 6, 7.5.
- Rear-delt fly, 7.5 lb per hand: 15, 15, 15 at RPE 6, 7, 8.
- Kettlebell swing, 40 lb: 8 × 10, RPE 7 on the first six, 7.5 on the last two.
- Daily hang logged with no figures.

**Pull-up history since September**
- 27 Sep: band pull-ups 5, 5 at RPE 6.
- 26 Oct: band pull-ups 6, 5, 5 at RPE 8.5; negatives 2, 2 at RPE 8 and 9; strict single at RPE 10.
- 1 Nov: band pull-ups 6, 6, 5, 4 at RPE 8, 8.5, 9.5, 10; strict single at RPE 10.

## 3. Warnings on this week's plan (the week of 2 Nov)

- **Circuit stacked on Monday**: the standing circuit was flagged as sitting on the same day as the overhead-press session. Already acknowledged: it is optional and Joe does it on a spare evening, never on top of Monday. Nothing to do.
- **Stall streaks** on overhead press, rear-delt fly, band pull-up, negative pull-up, both calf-raise lines, ab wheel, seated shoulder press and bent-over row: three logged sessions in a row with no gain on each line's progression measure (top-set strength for the press; reps added within the range for the others). These read the pre-engine history, so they are a record, not a verdict. Each clears the first time the line moves: more reps inside the range, a lighter band, or a heavier top set.
- **Rep range missed, band pull-up**: set 4 on 1 Nov came in at 4 reps at RPE 10, under the 5–8 range and over the effort cap, so the band stays where it is. Clears when all four sets land inside 5–8 at RPE 8 or under.
- **Loads held because there is no usable max** on the goblet squat (held at 20.25), chest-supported row (34), suitcase carry (4.25), seated shoulder press (22.5) and split squat (4.25). The engine can't check the RPE target against a max for these, so it leaves the load alone and goes by Joe's reps and RPE. They clear as history accumulates; no action needed, though the 4.25 carry figure and the 34 row figure look like placeholders worth a glance.
- **Suitcase carry logged at 0**: the logged load isn't a real plate row, so the engine used 5 instead. Clears when the actual bell weight is logged.
- **Squat pinned at 170.5**: more than one plate step above the anchor's 118. Already acknowledged: the anchor was a light home set, and the 13 Oct PT single of 100 kg puts 170.5 at about 75 % of his max, below what the scheme would have proposed. Nothing to do.
- **Hevy routine drift**: one Hevy routine no longer matches the approved plan (the reps on three sets of the first exercise and the weights on three sets of the second have been edited in the app; the pattern fits Monday's press and row). It resolves itself on the next weekly plan push, or by an override in that plan. Worth asking Joe whether he changed the routine deliberately.

## 4. The proposed amendment

The engine is now at a version that supports two things we worked around at cutover: a lift's target can count its training variants, and a weekday can hold two sessions. The draft was edited to use both. A dry run of adopting it shows:

**What it would record**
- Version 2 of the program, as an amendment: the current block (opened 1 Nov) continues, rotation stays in week A, nothing resets.
- **Pull-up target rises from 1 to 10 hard sets a week, with negatives and band pull-ups counting toward it.** The strict single stays the weekly measure under the same hold scheme. At present Wednesday supplies 3 negative sets and 4 band sets, so he would sit at about 7 of 10 until volume is added or a band is dropped.
- **The swing finisher leaves Monday's press session** (the 8 × 10 at 40 lb line is removed) and becomes **its own optional conditioning session scheduled beside Monday's lift**: a kettlebell swing EMOM, 12 minutes to start, 12 swings at the top of each minute at 40 lb, RPE target 7. When a session comes in at or under RPE 7, the engine adds 2 minutes, up to a cap of 16; after that, reps rise toward a cap of 15 per minute. Cues: hike it back, snap the hips, arms are ropes, bell floats to chest height.
- Monday's press session estimate drops from 58 to 47 minutes of its 75. Other estimates unchanged: Wednesday 39 of 75, Friday 65 of 75, Saturday 65 of 90, Sunday 65 of 90. All inside budget.
- The old acknowledgement for the pull-up's 1-set target is dropped, since the target is now inside the band.
- Start loads it would carry: swing 40 lb (18.14 kg in Hevy) in both the EMOM and the circuit; farmer's walk 50 lb (recorded in Hevy as 45.36 kg, which is both hands together).
- No defaults filled; everything is stated in the draft.

**Warnings after the change**
- **Deadlift target of 4 is outside the 5–15 band.** It was always 4, but the engine reports one off-band lift per version and the pull-up masked it. Two ways to clear it: raise the deadlift target to 5, or acknowledge it with a reason (for example, the PT sometimes programs deadlifts on Tuesday, which the target doesn't see). This needs a decision before adopting.
- **Strict pull-up on a hold scheme** rather than a progression scheme: already acknowledged (the single is the measure while his max is 1; negatives and band work do the building; it becomes real sets once he passes about five). Stays.
- **Hevy routine drift**: as above, independent of the amendment.

**What Joe needs to agree to**
1. Monday becomes two entries in Hevy: the press session, and a separate optional 12-minute swing EMOM that he can do straight after or on another evening. Skipping the EMOM never counts against adherence.
2. The pull-up target becomes 10 hard sets a week counting negatives and band pull-ups, which is the first honest measure of his pull-up volume; the Friday strict single stays exactly as it is.
3. Whether the deadlift target stays at 4 (acknowledged) or goes to 5.
4. Whether the edits to the Monday routine in Hevy were deliberate, so the next plan push doesn't overwrite something he wanted.

On his yes, the real adoption writes version 2; the Hevy routines themselves only change at the next weekly plan push.

first.text:
Here's what the change would do, checked before anything is recorded. Nothing is written yet; the programme on the books is still the one from 1 November.

**1. Pull-ups counted honestly.** Your pull-up target goes from 1 set a week to 10, and negatives and band pull-ups now count toward it. The Friday strict single stays exactly as it is: one max-effort rep, same grip every time, the measure rather than the training.

My reasoning for 10: it matches the weekly target every other muscle carries, so the lats are no longer the one muscle we pretend to under-train. Wednesday currently supplies 7 (3 sets of negatives, 4 of band pull-ups), so you'd sit a little under target until we add a set or you drop to a lighter band, and that gap is the point: it keeps a nudge on the one lift furthest behind. If you'd rather the number describe what you actually do today, 8 is the honest figure and still a legitimate target. Your call.

**2. Swings move out of Monday's press session.** The 8 × 10 at 40 lb finisher comes off the end of Monday and becomes its own optional conditioning piece sitting beside Monday's lifting: swings at the top of every minute, 12 minutes to start, 12 swings a minute at 40 lb, aiming for an effort of 7. Each time a session comes in at 7 or easier, it grows by 2 minutes up to 16; after that the reps climb toward 15 a minute. Cues: hike it back, snap the hips, arms are ropes, bell floats to chest height. Skipping it never counts against you. Monday's press session drops from about 58 to 47 minutes of its 75. Everything else stays where it was: Wednesday about 39 of 75, Friday 65 of 75, Saturday 65 of 90, Sunday 65 of 90.

Monday 2 November as you logged it stays untouched. Once this is adopted I'll confirm the swings have stopped counting as hard sets for your hamstrings and glutes; by design the new session is conditioning and shouldn't count, but I'll check rather than assume.

**3. The circuit.** Unchanged. This week's plan still carries the note about it sharing Monday, which you've already answered (optional, done on a spare evening). I can't confirm from here that the note is gone for good until next week's plan is built; I'll check then and tell you.

**One thing that needs a decision before I adopt.** Your deadlift target of 4 sets a week sits below the minimum the programme expects for a priority lift. It was always 4; the pull-up was the only one being reported, and fixing the pull-up has surfaced it. Two ways through: raise it to 5 (Sunday's top set and back-offs already give you that), or keep 4 with a stated reason, for example that your PT sometimes programmes deadlifts on Tuesday and that work isn't visible to the target. I lean to 5 so the number tells the truth without a footnote.

**Two other notes, independent of this change.**
- One of your Monday routines in the app has been edited by hand: the reps on three sets of the press and the weights on three sets of the row. Was that deliberate? The next weekly plan would overwrite it unless we carry the edits forward.
- Monday's press back-offs: you did sets of 8 where 6 were prescribed and called them easy. Good sign for the press; we'll let the top set catch up before adjusting anything.

I won't push anything to the app until you say the kit tables are ready; adopting only records the new version.

So: 10 or 8 on the pull-up target, 5 or 4-with-reason on the deadlift, and whether the Monday routine edits were yours. Say yes with those answers and I'll adopt.
